instantiated_cells.justification: The statute imposes periodic expenditure reporting obligations on registered principals (not lobbyists) and contains no requirement that lobbyists file an annual spending report.
Expense statements are required from principals on set dates, and no provision requires lobbyists to file monthly spending reports.
Reporting duties for lobbying expenditures are assigned to principals via the principal expense statement, not to lobbyists on any alternative schedule.
The only periodic spending report described is the principal’s semiannual expense statement; the statute does not require lobbyists to file quarterly spending reports.
Section 13.68 requires 'Every principal' registered to file the periodic expense statement, so the lobbyist is not the named filer of a separate semiannual spending report.
No statute provision requires lobbyists to file triannual reports linked to the legislative calendar; reporting is via principals’ semiannual statements.
Because the statute does not require any lobbyist-filed periodic spending report, there is no 'other' reporting frequency applicable to lobbyists.
Itemization duties in §13.68 apply to the principal’s expense statement, not a separate spending report filed by the lobbyist.
Principals file the semiannual expense statement while lobbyists only provide information for the principal’s filing, so lobbyists have no separate spending-report cadence ('none').
Section 13.67(1) requires the principal to report legislative proposals/topics, not the lobbyist as the filer of a separate report disclosing activity.

Although principals must report aggregate lobbying expenditures including compensation to lobbyists, the statute does not mandate that lobbyists themselves disclose earnings in a separate spending report.
The only contact-related time record requirement is imposed on principals in their expense statement; there is no lobbyist-filed contact disclosure report.
Per-issue/time allocation is required of principals for topics accounting for 10% or more of lobbying time, not as an expenditure-per-issue disclosure by lobbyists in a separate report.
General issues/topics must be reported by the principal to the commission, so there is no requirement for lobbyists to disclose general issues in a separate spending report.
Lobbying subjects are disclosed by principals under §13.67(1), and the statute does not create a lobbyist-filed activity report even at a general-subject level.
Required components for reporting expenditures are in the principal’s expense statement, not in a lobbyist’s own spending report covering gifts/entertainment/travel.
Indirect costs/overhead are disclosed by principals in their expense statement, and the statute does not require a lobbyist to file a separate report disclosing such costs.
Because lobbyists are not required to file their own itemized spending reports (they only provide signed information to principals), the described lobbyist-reporting regime does not exist.
While a license application may include a lobbyist’s residence address, the statute does not require lobbyists to disclose address/phone in a separate periodic spending report.
Disclosure of specific legislative proposals/topics is required from principals, not from lobbyists via a separate activity report.
The nature/purpose/business activity of the principal is disclosed in the principal’s registration statement, not as information the lobbyist must disclose in a separate spending report.
Principal address information is provided by the principal in its own registration statement, and there is no lobbyist-filed spending report requiring disclosure of principal address/phone.

Although a principal must file lobbyist authorizations and a lobbyist supplies information to the principal, the statute does not require lobbyists to file a separate report listing all principals represented.
Bill/proposal or rule numbers must be reported by the principal under §13.67(1), not by lobbyists in a separate spending report.
Direct lobbying costs including compensation are reported by the principal’s expense statement, not by a separate lobbyist-filed spending report.
Total lobbying expenditures are reported by principals in the semiannual expense statement, and there is no parallel requirement for lobbyists to file totals in their own report.
Because the statute does not require lobbyists to file spending reports (itemized or otherwise) and instead makes principals the filers, the answer is no.
The statute’s periodic filing obligation applies to registered principals regardless of spending; it does not impose a 'no activity' report obligation on lobbyists as separate filers.

Wisconsin’s lobbying reporting provisions assign expenditure reporting to principals rather than lobbyists, so there is no lobbyist spending report (including for household-member spending) required by the statute.

Any itemization requirements in Wisconsin are part of the principal’s expense statement, and the statute does not require lobbyists to disclose spending in any itemized-format report as separate filers.
